summary: Ernest Bender was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Temple University (~1937–1941) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1941–1949), where he later served as Professor of Indo-Aryan Languages and Literatures (~1950–1989).

Ernest Fenollosa worked in philosophy and Japanology after studying at Salem High School, Harvard College (~1870–1874), and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (~1876–1877). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1878–1886), MFA Boston (1890–1896), and University of Tsukuba (1897).

Ernest John Eitel was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1856–1860). He held posts with the London Missionary Society (~1865–1879) and at the University of Adelaide (~1897–1904).

Ernest Mackay worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Bristol Grammar School and the University of Bristol, and served at the Department of Antiquities (Mandatory Palestine) (~1919–1922).

Ernest Renan worked in religious studies, philosophy, and linguistics, studying at Saint-Sulpice Seminary (1843–1845) and the Collège de France (~1845–1848) under Eugène Burnouf (~1845–1852). He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and Collège de France (1861).

Ernest Sosa is a philosopher who studied at the University of Miami (~1958–1962) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1962–1964). He held posts as professor at Brown University (~1964–2007) and at Rutgers University (~2007).

Ernst Curtius was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the University of Bonn (~1833–1834) and University of Göttingen (~1834–1837). He held posts at Frederick William University / Humboldt University of Berlin (~1844–1896) and Göttingen (~1856–1868).

Ernst Gombrich worked in history and archaeology after studying at the Theresianum and the University of Vienna (~1928–1933). He held posts at the University of Vienna, the Warburg Institute (~1936–1976), and the University of London (~1956–1976).

Indologist Ernst Haas studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1854–1855) under Albrecht Weber, the University of Bonn (~1855–1856), and Tübingen (~1858–1859). He later served at the British Museum (1866) and as Professor of Sanskrit at University College London (1875).

Ernst Kuhn worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at Berlin, Tübingen, Leipzig, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth, he held posts at Heidelberg University (~1871–1877) and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1877–1920).
Ernst Leumann was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He held professorial posts at the University of Strasbourg from ~1884 to 1897 and ~1897 to 1919.

Ernst Steinkellner works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1956–1963) under Erich Frauwallner (~1957–1963) and held posts at Vienna (~1964–1970, attested 1981–2014), Kyoto University (1982), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1991–2005).
Ernst Trumpp worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying under Rudolf von Roth (~1848–1853), he served as professor at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1874–1885).

Ernst Waldschmidt was an Indologist and specialist in Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied under Heinrich Lüders, August Hermann Francke, and Albert Grünwedel (~1920–1924) and at Göttingen (1924), later holding posts at Göttingen (1936–1965) and its Academy (1936).

Ernst Windisch, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Leipzig University (1863–1868) under Georg Curtius, Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, Friedrich Zarncke, and Hermann Brockhaus. He held chairs at Heidelberg (1872), Strasbourg (1875), and Leipzig (1871–1918), and led the DMG (~1903–1918).

Erwin Rousselle worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts at Peking University (~1924–1930), Tsinghua University (~1925–1930), Yenching University (~1930–1931), and Goethe University Frankfurt (1935).
Esben Andreasen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Copenhagen. He was a visiting researcher at Otani University in 1992.

Eshin Nishimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. at Kyoto University (~1957–1963). He held posts at Carleton College (~1967–1968) and served at Hanazono University as researcher, professor, and director (~1969–2009).
Esho Kawasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as director at the Buddhist Cultural Institute (attested 1999) and president at Kyushu Ryukoku Gakkai (attested 2002).
Esho Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who held posts at Ikenobo Junior College (attested 1979) and as professor at Kyoto Women's University (attested 1991).
